name: Malcolm Tan
life: “I still remember a work lunch carried in the very last family tin.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Malcolm by a small Saturday habit. Malcolm checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I brought an empty milk tin from the shop my parents lost. I finally heard something new inside it.
appearance: Malcolm has a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Look for short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a black overshirt with pearl buttons with a small enamel bird on the lapel. In conversation Malcolm presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Malcolm treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Malcolm lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To get the old milk tin into the program.
family: Cian Malik is Malcolm’s second cousin. Malcolm can always ask for five minutes alone. Cian asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The broken till*, Cian says, “I recognized my first boss's pencil shorthand.”
connections: Howard Heller. Keys and the old packing tin place a shop closing inside the music.

reactions.situation: An instrument breaks before the fountain piece begins
reactions.response: Malcolm asks the player whether a different everyday object can carry the missing note.

reactions.situation: A family supper turns into an argument about old debt
reactions.response: Malcolm clears the dishes, lets the angriest speaker cool off, and resumes the conversation with a smaller audience.

reactions.situation: When offered a favor with ambiguous terms
reactions.response: Malcolm says what can be returned and asks whether that will do.
